clue.text: I am and so was Adam

definitions.meaning: in grammar the pronoun I and its verb form am belong to the speaker's own category of person
in the Bible Adam was the earliest human being created, the original man

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves define the answer: grammatically 'I am' is in the first person, and Adam, the earliest man, was literally the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical label for the speaker, and also a phrase for the very earliest human, which Genesis makes Adam.

clue.text: Anticipated war foes' belligerence

indicators.note: belligerence is aggressive fighting, so the letters of the words beside it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone foresaw that enemies would come to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belligerence' is the anagram signal, applied to the seven letters of WAR FOES (the apostrophe adds nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: To have anticipated something is to have seen it coming in advance.

clue.text: Gloria takes part of lasso

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman named Gloria joins in with some rope work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' signals a run of letters hiding in 'Gloria takes': gloRIA TAkes.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a cowboy's long rope with a running noose, the same thing as a lariat or lasso.

clue.text: Actor accepted a small measure of syrup

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it in, so the actor's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager, a crossword favourite
cl is the abbreviation for centilitre, a small measure of liquid

explanation.surface: A performer takes a small spoonful of syrup, perhaps as medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' is the stock crossword reference to Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the Victorian actor-manager; 'accepted' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the British name for a dark sugar syrup, as in golden syrup or molasses.

clue.text: Expeditionary force leaders' story capable of being expressed

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their opening letters, one taken from each

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: Army commanders tell a tale that can be put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders'' takes the first letters of 'Expeditionary' and 'force', giving EF.
explanation.definitionFit: Effable is the rare opposite of ineffable: something that can be uttered or described in words.

clue.text: Unimportant crook?

definitions.meaning: petty, minor, operating on a modest scale
the question mark hints at the phrase completing the word crook, a petty criminal of the minor sort

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is straight; the second is cryptic, leaning on the everyday phrase for a petty criminal, which the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time means minor or petty, and a small-time crook is the standard phrase for a lowly criminal.

clue.text: Unclear about a form of energy

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective naming that form, as in power from atoms

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the seven letters of the word next to it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure what a particular kind of energy is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to rearrange UNCLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power, released by splitting or fusing atoms, is a recognised kind of energy alongside solar and wind.

clue.text: Caterer upset in domestic row

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of the caterer are scrambled

explanation.surface: A distressed caterer gets caught up in a household quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic row' looks like a quarrel at home, but here it is a row of houses; 'upset' rearranges CATERER.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace in Britain is a row of joined houses, so a row of homes.

clue.text: Getting into form

parts.note: reads like someone getting fit again, but means something developing into a definite shape or outline

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an athlete regaining fitness; the answer describes plans or objects becoming definite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something developing its final outline is said to be acquiring its shape, i.e. coming together.

clue.text: Man — he is left out of licence to sell company's products

indicators.note: when letters are left out of a word, they are removed from it

parts.note: a franchise is the right granted to sell a firm's goods or services
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is excluded from a sales licence agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' removes H and E (not side by side) from FRANCHISE; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis is a common male first name, so a man in crossword terms.

clue.text: Eye, subject upon which agitation is concentrated

definitions.meaning: the calm centre of a hurricane or cyclone

definitions.text: subject upon which agitation is concentrated
definitions.meaning: figuratively, the focus of trouble or controversy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' is the meteorological sense, the middle of a storm; the second definition is the figurative focus of unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists call the middle of a cyclone its eye; figuratively it is the focal point of any turmoil.

clue.text: Kelvin has a new dish

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin, the SI unit of temperature

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the words before it made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man called Kelvin has cooked up something new to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kelvin' is not a man here but the temperature unit's symbol; 'new' rearranges HAS to give ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Kasha is a porridge of buckwheat or other grain eaten in Eastern Europe, a dish in its own right.

clue.text: Spaniard put everything into circular trunk first

indicators.note: first says the trunk comes before the round letter in the answer
putting one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: a caber is the tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games
everything means all
a circle looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman is told to put all his belongings in a round chest first.
explanation.walkthrough: A caber is the pole tossed at Scottish Highland games; 'first' says that trunk, with its contents, precedes the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A caballero is a Spanish gentleman or horseman, so a Spaniard.

clue.text: Was acquainted with, say, swell music

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than read, so the phrase before it is spoken

parts.note: to have known someone is to have been acquainted with them
a swell is a long rolling wave at sea

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being familiar with some great music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you KNEW is heard, giving NEW; 'swell' looks like an old word for 'great' but is a sea wave.
explanation.definitionFit: New wave was a late-1970s style of pop and rock music that followed punk.

clue.text: Stopping at sea

parts.note: read literally, a ship halting in open water by dropping a heavy hook to hold it in place

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads like halting mid-voyage; the answer is the act of mooring a vessel by lowering its hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship comes to rest away from port by lowering its heavy iron hook to the seabed.

clue.text: Witty saying with a note on farm animals

parts.note: E is one of the notes of the musical scale
a pig is a farm animal
a ram, a male sheep, is a farm animal too

explanation.surface: A remark is passed around with a written note about livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farm animals' gives two pieces, PIG and RAM; E is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short clever remark or pithy verse, a quip.

clue.text: Seek after it coils round

indicators.note: after places the anagram before the little word, which follows it
round means moved in a circle, so the letters of the word next to it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes looking for something after it winds itself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seek after' reads as one phrase, but 'Seek' alone is the definition; 'round' scrambles the coils to SOLIC, and 'after' sets that before the closing two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for or try to obtain something, as in soliciting donations.

clue.text: Begin to play leaving deb out of disastrous double date

indicators.note: the word after leaving is something abandoned, so its letters are taken away
out of says the letters are removed from the following phrase
disastrous signals a mess, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A debutante walks out of a calamitous evening out with two couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' scrambles DOUBLE DATE; 'leaving' and 'out of' remove the letters of DEB from that pool, and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games or sport, to lead out is to make the opening play.

clue.text: Reportedly make an attempt with hollow spear

indicators.note: reportedly says this part is heard, so what is spoken is a word for trying

parts.note: to make an attempt is to try
a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have a go with a spear that is empty inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns TRY into the sound TRI. 'hollow' looks like an adjective for the spear but is a noun giving DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune.

clue.text: New rep be confronted with introduction

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of the following word made into a fresh order

parts.note: to face something is to be confronted with it

explanation.surface: A newly hired sales representative has to meet the introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges REP to PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the opening section of a book, an introductory statement.

clue.text: Make a stab at joke first by one Indian

indicators.note: first puts the joke at the head of the answer, ahead of the stabbing action

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
to jab is to stab or poke at
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a joke before an Indian audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a stab at' looks like 'try' but means JAB; 'first' puts PUN ahead of it, and 'by' joins I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Punjabi is a person from the Punjab region of northern India and Pakistan.

clue.text: So certain number had life policy

parts.note: so and as are interchangeable in comparisons
certain means sure
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a number

explanation.surface: Someone so sure of themselves had taken out life cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So certain' looks like the definition but is wordplay; the number is 500 in Roman numerals. In British usage life cover is called assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, life cover is called assurance, so someone who held a life policy was assured.

clue.text: Strong woman with Scotsman coming from the river

indicators.note: coming from puts the Scotsman after the river in the answer, as if he emerged from it

parts.note: the Amazon is the great river of South America
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A powerful woman and a Scot emerge from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the stock crossword Scotsman; 'coming from' sets him after the river, as if he emerged from it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Amazons were a race of women warriors, so the adjective describes a tall powerful woman.

clue.text: Assume one is in employment

indicators.note: one thing that is in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a post is a job or position of employment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes it for granted they have a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' puts I inside POST.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, i.e. to take as given.

clue.text: To an important person getting up — it is the turning-point

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means read from the bottom, so the whole run is backwards

parts.note: VIP stands for very important person

explanation.surface: Someone rises to meet a dignitary at a decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns the whole of TO plus VIP, which in a down answer reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the pin or point on which something turns, so the point of rotation.

clue.text: Egghead had reason to be excitable

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter, E
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: An intellectual had grounds for being worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but is just the first letter of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means arousing feeling, close to being charged or stirred up.

clue.text: Notice few lines that are hostile

parts.note: an ad is a notice, as in a newspaper advertisement
a verse is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A notice of a few lines turns out to be unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' is a noun here, an advertisement, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means unfavourable or opposing, as in adverse conditions.

clue.text: Mean and looking ready for a fight

definitions.meaning: literally with hands clenched into fists

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is stinginess; the second takes the phrase literally, with fists clenched as before a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy people grip their money hard, and a fighter clenches both hands before throwing punches.
